headline: Revenue growth stays strong, GAAP profit normalizes
summary_short: Axon reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $904M, up 35.3% y/y and 12.0% q/q, its tenth straight quarter of 30%+ growth. Net income of $29M and diluted EPS of $0.36 fell sharply q/q and y/y only because prior quarters included a $189M investment gain and a $75M tax benefit; pretax income still rose y/y.
summary_long: Software & Services revenue rose 36% y/y to $398M on AI Era Plan adoption; Connected Devices grew 35% to $507M on Dedrone, TASER 10 and Axon Body 4. Gross margin was flat y/y at 60.4%, up 130bp q/q. GAAP operating income rose to $47M from a $1M loss y/y. Net income and EPS fell q/q and y/y only because prior quarters included a $189M investment gain and a $75M tax benefit; pretax income still grew y/y. Adjusted EBITDA of $242M (26.8% margin) rose over 40% y/y. Operating cash flow improved to $20M from a $92M outflow. Cash and investments fell to $673M from $719M q/q. Axon raised FY2026 revenue-growth guidance to 32-34% and kept its EBITDA-margin and capex outlooks.

drivers.explanation: Company cites its tenth consecutive quarter of 30%+ revenue growth, driven by broad-based demand across Software & Services and Connected Devices plus record bookings and ARR.
Software & Services grew 36% y/y on AI Era Plan and Axon 911 adoption; Connected Devices grew 35% y/y on Dedrone, TASER 10 and Axon Body 4.
Adjusted gross margin slipped 40bp y/y on a higher professional-services mix and new-product scaling, partly offset by global tariff refunds received in the quarter, per management.
COGS grew with volume and a mix shift toward Dedrone and professional services, partially offset by tariff refunds received in the quarter.
Increase driven by higher revenue and global tariff refunds, partially offset by continued investment to drive future growth, per management.

This Yahoo-provenance figure embeds 'other income, net,' only $7M this quarter versus a $189M investment gain booked there in Q1 FY2026 — the q/q drop is a comparison-base effect, not weaker operations.
Same Q1 FY2026 $189M investment-gain base effect drives the q/q decline; management's own Adjusted EBITDA of $242M (26.8% margin) rose over 40% y/y and is the cleaner read.
Q1 FY2026 pretax income included the $189M investment gain; excluding that base effect, pretax income actually rose year over year per the release.
Company states the y/y decline primarily reflects a large tax benefit recognized in Q2 FY2025, not a change in pre-tax profitability, which rose year over year.
Improvement to a $20M inflow from a $92M outflow y/y was driven by higher EBITDA, partly offset by inventory investment and billing/collection timing, per management.
Cash and short-term investments combined fell to $673M from $719M q/q and from $2,087M a year ago, mostly reflecting Q1 FY2026's roughly $550M of acquisitions.
Increase driven mainly by $29M of net income plus a $100M equity offering completed during the quarter, per the release and balance sheet.
